title: Gratuity Tax Rules: Understanding Your Tax-Free Limit
description: Gratuity is a lump sum payment from an employer as a token of appreciation for long and dedicated service. To be eligible, an employee typically needs to comp.

faq.q: What is the primary purpose of gratuity?
faq.a: Gratuity is a statutory benefit paid by an employer to an employee as a token of appreciation for long and dedicated service. It is a lump sum payment made upon termination of employment, providing a financial cushion.

No, gratuity is not always fully tax-free. While gratuity for government employees is fully exempt, for private sector employees, there's a maximum tax-exempt limit of ₹20 lakhs, and the actual exempt amount is calculated based on specific rules.

faq.q: Do I need to complete 5 years of service to receive gratuity?
faq.a: Generally, yes, a minimum of five years of continuous service is required for gratuity eligibility under The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972. However, this condition is waived in cases of death or disablement, where gratuity is payable irrespective of service length.

faq.q: How does the ₹20 lakh limit apply to gratuity?
faq.a: The ₹20 lakh limit is the maximum amount of gratuity that can be exempt from income tax for private sector employees, as notified by the Central Government. The actual exempt amount will be the least of the actual gratuity received, ₹20 lakh, or the amount calculated by specific formulas.

faq.q: What happens if I receive gratuity from multiple employers?
faq.a: If you receive gratuity from more than one employer, either in the same financial year or across different financial years, the aggregate of the tax-exempt gratuity from all employers cannot exceed the overall statutory limit of ₹20 lakhs.

faq.q: Is gratuity considered part of my salary for tax purposes?
faq.a: The taxable portion of your gratuity, if any, is considered "income from salaries" and is added to your total income for the financial year in which it is received. It is then taxed at your applicable income tax slab rates.

faq.q: Can I claim any deductions on the taxable portion of gratuity?
faq.a: No, there are no specific deductions available against the taxable portion of gratuity. It is simply added to your 'income from salaries' and taxed as per your income tax slab, without further exemptions or deductions.
